questions.question: Calculate the distance (in cm) of the chord from the centre of the circle, if the chord of length 48 cm is drawn in the circle of radius 25 cm.
questions.solution:
**Detailed solution:-**

The given figure can be drawn as,

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d55281845beabdcc406e5864df3ab210af20e625326dc3ea5b0cfd3561ebf7f.png] **

Let O be the centre of the circle, AB be the chord and P is the centre point of chord AB, such that OP is the distance of the chord from the centre of the circle

Now, OA = OB = radius of circle = 25 cm

Length of chord = AB = 48 cm

⇒ PB = AB/2 = 48/2 = 24 cm

Applying Pythagoras theorem in ΔOPB,

⇒ OB² = OP² + PB²

⇒ 25² = OP² + 24²

⇒ OP² = 625 - 576 = 49

⇒ OP = √49 = 7 cm

**∴ Distance of chord from centre of circle =__ 7__ cm**

questions.question:
If the angle subtended by the radius of a circle (OB) and the side BC of the triangle ABC at vertex B is 40° then calculate the value of ∠BAC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88fa25ea54a10ce3ee1b13cc5b76318ea32d0eb2ee8d243679240f9082d0e881.png]
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In ΔOBC, OB = OC (radii of the circle), so ∠OCB = ∠OBC = 40°.

Angle at the center: ∠BOC = 180° − (40° + 40°) = 100°.

Angle at the circumference: ∠BAC = ∠BOC ÷ 2 = 100° ÷ 2 = 50°.

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠OBC = 40°

OB is the radius of the circle with center O.

**Formula Used:**

1. In an isosceles triangle, angles opposite to equal sides are equal.

2. The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67a8d07fd492597edc548a4401b32b8b4e0ab0d37fa109539e31e8405c73fee6.png] 

**Calculations:**

In ΔOBC:

⇒ OB = OC (since both are radii of the same circle)

⇒ ∠OCB = ∠OBC = 40° (angles opposite to equal sides are equal)

We know that the sum of angles in a triangle is 180°:

⇒ ∠BOC + ∠OBC + ∠OCB = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC + 40° + 40° = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC + 80° = 180°

⇒ ∠BOC = 180° − 80° = 100°

By the circle theorem, the angle subtended by arc BC at the center O is twice the angle subtended at the circumference at A:

⇒ ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC

⇒ 100° = 2 × ∠BAC

⇒ ∠BAC = 100° ÷ 2

⇒ ∠BAC = 50°

**Option Verification:**

⇒ **Option (1) 35°:** Incorrect, as this would imply ∠BOC = 70°, which means ∠OBC + ∠OCB = 110°, making each 55° instead of the given 40°.

⇒ **Option (2) 45°:** Incorrect, as this would imply ∠BOC = 90°, which means ∠OBC + ∠OCB = 90°, making each 45° instead of the given 40°.

⇒ **Option (3) 50°:** Correct, as it perfectly satisfies ∠BOC = 100° and ∠OBC = ∠OCB = 40°.

⇒ **Option (4) 65°:** Incorrect, as this would imply ∠BOC = 130°, which means ∠OBC + ∠OCB = 50°, making each 25° instead of the given 40°.

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc or chord at any points on the remaining part of the circle are equal to each other.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180°.</p

questions.question: Weights of two friends A and B are in the ratio of 7 : 8. A’s weight increases by 10% and the total weight of A and B increase by 20%. What is the percentage increase in the B’s weight?
questions.solution:
Let the initial weight of A and B be ‘7x’ and ‘8x’ units respectively

Total weight of A & B = 7x + 8x = 15x

When A’s weight increases by 10% & total weight increases by 20%,

⇒ A’s increased weight = 110% of 7x = 1.1 × 7x = 7.7x

⇒ Total increased weight = 120% of 15x = 1.2 × 15x = 18x

Hence,

B’s increased weight = 18x - 7.7x = 10.3x

⇒ Increase in B’s weight = 10.3x - 8x = 2.3x

∴ Percentage increase in B’s weight = 2.3x/8x × 100 = 28.75%

questions.question: The income of X, Y and Z are in the ratio of 3 : 4 : 2 and their expenses in the ratio of 5 : 5 : 2. If X saves Rs. 3000 out of an income of Rs. 18000, then what will be the saving (in Rs.) of Y?
questions.solution:
Given, X’s income = Rs. 18000

But, X’s income ∶ Y’s income = 3 ∶ 4

⇒ 18000/Y’s income = 3/4

⇒ Y’s income = 18000 × 4/3 = Rs. 24000

Now, X’s savings = Rs. 3000

∵ Expenses = Income - Savings

⇒ X’s expenses = 18000 - 3000 = Rs. 15000

But, X’s expenses ∶ Y’s expenses = 5 ∶ 5

⇒ 15000/Y’s expenses = 1

⇒ Y’s expenses = Rs. 15000

∴ Y’s savings = 24000 - 15000 = Rs. 9000

questions.question: P and Q are two alloys which are prepared by mixing tin and lead in the ratio of 12 : 5 and 4 : 3 respectively. If equal quantities of alloys are melted to form a third alloy R, then what is the ratio of tin and lead in alloy R?
questions.solution:
Let ‘x’ units of P and Q alloys are melted to form third alloy

Tin-lead ratio in P alloy = 12 ∶ 5

⇒ Quantity of Tin in ‘x’ units of P alloy = (12/17)x

⇒ Quantity of Lead in ‘x’ units of P alloy = (5/17)x

Similarly,

Tin-lead ratio in Q alloy = 4 ∶ 3

⇒ Quantity of Tin in ‘x’ units of Q alloy = (4/7)x

⇒ Quantity of Lead in ‘x’ units of Q alloy = (3/7)x

Hence,

Total quantity of Tin in R alloy = (12/17)x + (4/7)x = (152/119)x

Total quantity of Lead in R alloy = (5/17)x + (3/7)x = (86/119)x

∴ Tin-lead ratio in R alloy = (152x/119) ∶ (86x/119) = 152 ∶ 86 = 76 ∶ 43

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 20 years is 5/4 of the principal. What is the per annum rate (in percentage) of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The simple interest on a sum for 20 years is 5/4 of the principal.

**Concept used:**

Simple interest = PRT/100

**Calculation:**

Given, time = 20 years

⇒ (5/4)P = (P × R × 20)/100

⇒ R = 5/4 × 5 = 25/4

**∴ The rate of interest is 6.25% p.a.**

questions.question: If Mohan purchase 13 articles for Rs. 12 and sells all the articles at the rate of 12 articles for Rs. 13, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Detailed solution:-**

Cost price of 13 articles = Rs. 12

⇒ Cost price of 1 article = Rs. 12/13

Similarly,

Selling price of 12 articles = Rs. 13

⇒ Selling price of 1 article = Rs. 13/12

∵ Profit = Selling price - Cost price

⇒ Profit on 1 article = 13/12 - 12/13 = Rs. 25/156

∴ Profit percentage = (25/156)/(12/13) × 100 = 25/144 × 100 = 17.36%

Robin can do a work alone in 9 days. Amit can do the same work alone in 6 days. Both of them finish the work together and they get a total Rs. 2500. What is the share (in Rs.) of Robin?
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

(1) Robin can do work alone in 9 days

(2) Amit can do the same work alone in 6 days.

**Detailed solution:-**

Robin’s 1-day work = 1/9

Amit’s 1-day work = 1/6

When they work together, they received Rs. 2500

∵ The ratio of wages = Ratio of work efficiencies

⇒ Robin’s share∶ Amit’s share = (1/9) ∶ (1/6) = 6 ∶ 9 = 2 ∶ 3

Sum of ratios = 2 + 3 = 5

∴ Robin’s share = 2/5 × 2500 = Rs. 1000

questions.question: A boat covers 63 km upstream in 9 hours and covers the same distance downstream in 7 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
**Given:-** 

(1) A boat covers 63 km upstream in 9 hours 

(2) covers the same distance downstream in 7 hours

**Formula used:-**

Speed = Distance/time 

**Calculation:-**

Upstream speed = Distance/time = 63/9 = 7 km/hr

Downstream speed = Distance/time = 63/7 = 9 km/hr

∵ Speed in still water = 1/2 × (Upstream speed + Downstream speed)

**∴ Speed of boat in still water = (9 + 7)/2 = 8 km/hr**

questions.question: The lengths of the two diagonals of a rhombus are 5 cm and 12 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

Diagonals = 5 cm & 12 cm

**Formula used:-**

Area of rhombus = 1/2 × Product of its diagonals

**Calculation:-**

As we know,

Area of rhombus = 1/2 × Product of its diagonals

∴ Area of rhombus = (5 × 12)/2 = 30 cm²

questions.question: What is the sum of the measures of all the interior angles of a regular polygon of 9 sides?
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

The sum of the measures of all the interior angles of a regular polygon of 9 sides

**Formula used:-**

The sum of interior angles = (n - 2) 180°

**Calculation:-**

For a regular polygon with n sides,

The sum of interior angles = (n - 2) 180°

∴ Sum of interior angles of a regular polygon with 9 sides = (9 - 2) × 180° = 1260° 

**∴The required answer is 1260°.**

questions.question: ΔPQR is right angled at Q. If ∠R = 60°, then find the value of (sec P - 1/√3).
questions.solution:
**Detailed solution:-**

Given, in ∆PQR, ∠Q = 90° and ∠R = 60°

The sum of angles of a triangle = 180°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R = 180°

⇒ ∠P + 90° + 60° = 180°

⇒ ∠P = 180° - 150° = 30°

∴ (sec P - 1/√3) = sec 30° - 1/√3 = 2/√3 - 1/√3 = 1/√3
